maria-ops: Heads up—after deploying the kernel selector tweak in canary we see subtle output drift on reshape-heavy inference traces. Only happens when activation path uses BF16->FP8 mixed matmul with per-channel calibration. Not a latency regression (perf stable) but correctness mismatch vs fp16 baseline. :eyes:

devon-runtime: repro? sample input + seed?

maria-ops: minimal repro attached, run: ```python repro.py --model redwood/xxl --quant bf8_channel --seed 42 --batch 8``` Outputs diverge at token ~12 vs fp16 baseline, KL delta ~1e-2. Logs show different scale applied after a reshape+transpose in attention projection.

shivani-ml: could be KV cache shaping + cached prefix being quantized with old scale. Did you try disabling prefix cache? Also which calibration mode—per-channel or per-tensor?

maria-ops: per-channel calibration. Disabling KV cache makes it go away for short traces, but long-context runs still misalign. Seems tied to matmul selection when seq_len > 128 and batching heuristics flip kernel. Repro: ```TRACE=1 ./serve --route=/generate --batch_threshold=4``` Kernel selection logs: `selected kernel: matmul_fp8_block32_transpose_optimized` then later `selected kernel: matmul_bf16_pointwise` on other shards.

ryan-eng: dropping small unit test showing the mismatch: ```assert_allclose(out_fp16, out_mixed, rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-4)``` fails at index [0,12]. Stack: attention.proj @ matmul_kernel.cu:234. Suspect scale multiplication order around reshape: scale applied before transpose not after.

perf-bot: perf alert: throughput stable (+1%), p99 latency unchanged, correctness delta triggered by eval harness (regression id rg-2026-03-17-9). Link: https://ci.internal/reports/rg-2026-03-17-9

devon-runtime: can you paste the raw tensor metadata (shapes, dtype, quant params) around the failing op?

maria-ops: ```tensor_name: attn_proj; shape: [8,512,1024]; dtype: fp8_e4m3; scale: [512]; quant_axis: 2; layout: [B,S,H]; after reshape -> [8,8,64,1024] transpose(2,3) -> scale still length 512 but now axis mapping changed``` Looks like kernel expects per-channel scale on last dim but layout change moved the channel axis.

shivani-ml: aha—per-channel scales are not being permuted with the tensor layout during reshape/transpose. The FP8 kernel assumes scale alignment with dim -1. Some mixed-precision matmuls do implicit flatten/unflatten that lost axis metadata. That's a bug in kernel selection/metadata propagation.

ryan-eng: quick mitigation: force fallback to fp16/bf16 matmul for ops where reshapes/transposes change channel axis. Patch idea: runtime check in kernel-selector: if quantized and permute_changes_axis(quant_axis) then prefer non-quant kernel or reorder scales accordingly.

maria-ops: test patch: added guard + fallback, re-ran eval, regression disappeared. Perf impact ~+6% token cost on affected workloads but correctness restored. Will open PR with test and repro.

devon-runtime: we'll need a proper fix that either permutes scale tensors when layout transforms happen or have the quant kernels accept axis arg. Also add an assert in debug builds to catch scale/tensor misalignment.

shivani-ml: also check KV cache write path—cached kv entries may be stored without recording effective scale after a kernel switch. If cache writers assume last-used scale, that'll silently corrupt later retrievals.

maria-ops: noted. I'll add a write that stores scale meta with cached blocks. For now PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pull/3245 (draft)

ryan-eng: thanks. I'll pick this up after standup, bisect suggests regression introduced by commit c3f9a7 (kernel-selector heuristics) — assigning to @devon-runtime and @maria-ops. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: NOTE: schedule a perf/regression eval run for the PR. ```/schedule-eval rg-2026-03-17-9``` 

maria-ops: adding unit tests and a small integration harness. Will coordinate with infra to run on GPU matrix sizes earlier than 128 and >128 to cover kernel flip. Thanks.

devon-runtime: good catch. keep thread updated.
